strengths: Clearly identifies and formalizes an important, understudied problem (contextual contradictions in text-to-image generation) with well-motivated examples and intuitive motivation

Comprehensive experimental validation across three benchmarks with quantitative (GPT-4o alignment, Table 1), qualitative (Figures 6-15), and user study components (1,464 evaluations); demonstrates consistent 4-6% improvements in alignment
Sound methodology naturally aligned with diffusion process structure (coarse-to-fine decomposition); clear intuition for why stage-aware injection helps resolve conceptual conflicts
Training-free and practical approach requiring no model retraining; seamlessly integrates with existing FLUX and SD3.0 models; demonstrates robustness across different LLMs (Table 5)
Thorough reproducibility with detailed LLM instructions, full benchmark construction details, VLM evaluation protocol, and in-context examples provided; enables future work
Honest failure analysis with categorization of failure modes (Table 7) and discussion of method limitations; ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrate importance of key components
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: LLM-based decomposition and stage-aware prompt injection are straightforward applications of existing techniques; main contribution is problem formulation rather than algorithmic innovation
Modest empirical improvements: Table 1 shows 4-6% gains over baselines, which while consistent, are incremental rather than transformative; lacking statistical significance testing

Evaluation methodological concerns: (1) GPT-4o alignment metric is somewhat subjective (Table 13 scoring rubric has interpretive aspects); (2) User study samples only 24 of 40 ContraBench prompts; (3) Missing comparisons with simpler alternatives (naive multi-stage prompting, non-decomposed LLM re-prompting)

Narrow problem scope with unclear generalization: ContraBench contains only 40 ChatGPT-generated prompts (potential construction bias); method fails on ~33% of cases (Table 7); applicability to open-ended contradictions and diverse contradiction types unclear

Insufficient technical justification: (1) Stage selection (Table 8) lacks ablation studies; (2) Why coarse-to-fine alignment resolves conceptual conflicts not rigorously analyzed; (3) Decomposition arbitrariness evident in Table 10 examples; (4) No analysis of proxy prompt fidelity to intermediate semantics

Limited analysis of method behavior: No computational cost quantification; missing correlation between decomposition complexity and success rate; baseline methods (R2F, Annealing) tuning details absent; evaluation limited to FLUX/SD3.0—robustness to other architectures unknown

Generalization limitations: Problem-specific to certain prompt types; method entirely dependent on base model capabilities; only visual synthesis tested; no evaluation of diversity-quality trade-offs or cross-style evaluation
Presentation issues: Figures 13-15 have dense text with readability problems; limited discussion of theoretical underpinnings; some design choices appear ad-hoc rather than principled

strengths: Clear problem identification: Contextual contradictions are articulated as a specific, understandable failure mode in text-to-image generation with intuitive examples
Well-motivated technical approach: Using coarse-to-fine diffusion dynamics to inject stage-specific prompts is sensible and grounded in model behavior
Comprehensive evaluation setup: Multiple datasets (Whoops!, ContraBench), user studies, ablation studies, and failure analysis demonstrate experimental rigor in methodology
Training-free practicality: Method works with pretrained models without retraining, improving applicability
Detailed transparency: Full LLM prompts (Tables 8-10), decomposition examples, and failure mode breakdown (Table 7) aid reproducibility
weaknesses: Marginal quantitative improvements: SAP achieves only 0.47-point gain over baselines on primary benchmark (83.10 vs 82.63 on Whoops!), with user study showing 62.13% alignment—barely above chance for added complexity

Limited technical novelty: Core contribution reduces to applying known techniques (LLM guidance, stage-aware prompt injection); insufficient differentiation from prior LLM-guided diffusion and multi-prompt conditioning work
Critical bottleneck unresolved: Table 7 reveals 63.3% of failures stem from proxy assignment, yet paper offers no principled solution, suggesting the fundamental limitation remains

Weak empirical validation: User study involves only 24 prompts and 51 participants with no statistical significance testing; GPT-4o alignment as primary metric lacks validation against actual image quality
Reproducibility concerns: Heavy reliance on proprietary GPT-4o (version-dependent), incomplete in-context examples, limited validation across alternative LLMs (Appendix only), no code availability

Fuzzy problem scope: 'Contextual contradiction' lacks formal definition; distinction from general prompt misalignment unclear; problem is relatively niche with unclear impact on overall text-to-image generation
Insufficient baselines: Only compares against 2-3 relevant methods; missing comparisons with recent prompt optimization techniques and simpler alternatives
Limited theoretical justification: No formal analysis of why stage-specific decomposition outperforms standard injection; timestep assignment mechanism and sensitivity analysis incomplete

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear examples of contextual contradictions in text-to-image generation
Practical, training-free solution applicable to existing diffusion models without architectural modifications
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including quantitative metrics (GPT-4o alignment), user studies (81% vs 63-78% baseline alignment), ablation studies, and robustness analysis
Consistent empirical improvements across multiple datasets (Whoops!, Whoops-Hard, ContraBench) and diverse baselines
Clear presentation with effective visualizations that clearly demonstrate the problem and solution
Transparent discussion of limitations and failure modes with detailed categorization
Thorough documentation in appendices supporting reproducibility with full LLM instructions and benchmark specifications
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily combines existing techniques (LLM reasoning, stage-aware injection, diffusion denoising) in straightforward manner; individual components not novel
Heavy dependence on LLM quality with limited robustness analysis across different models; computational overhead not quantified
Evaluation scope limitations: ContraBench contains only 40 prompts, user study on ~24 prompts, focus on visual contradictions limits generalization claims
Incomplete baseline comparisons lacking alternative prompt engineering approaches, negative prompting strategies, or other reasoning-based methods
Methodological concerns: GPT-4o alignment metric is indirect, timestep interval assignment appears heuristic-based, limited justification for specific diffusion stage selection
Vague characterization of failure modes (33.3% 'model limitation' failures, 63.3% 'proxy assignment' failures) with only 40 failure cases analyzed
Limited analysis of computational costs and practical deployment considerations; no wall-clock time comparisons provided
Narrow scope specific to contradictory prompts; unclear generalization to other generation failure modes or cross-lingual settings
